| [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) | A producer's own rate of return is the price of their time, so making them faster raises the bar on every marginal hour of improvement | Duede, Gross, Crockett and Bergstrom (2026), [LIT-492](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-492.md) — in a marginal-value-theorem model of effort allocation, the long-run rate of return is simultaneously the objective and the opportunity cost of the marginal hour. Any acceleration raises it, so the marginal hour of improvement has to clear a higher bar. Whether quality then falls is a race between that bar and the value of the hour, which is why the sign depends on **which phase** was accelerated rather than on how much time was saved. | Proposed |
